record.scope: Local configuration, credential helper, child ownership, managed-session and process-startup trust boundaries in both clients; production local sources shared identically.

findings.severity: Low (local configuration integrity; no remote exploit or cross-account privilege escalation established)
findings.title: --init-config could overwrite a concurrently created configuration
findings.cause: main loaded a missing config, then called the ordinary replacing config_save path. Its final renameat could replace a file created after the absence check.
findings.impact: Concurrent initialization or saving could silently discard another newly created config, including credential references or inline credentials, despite never-overwrite help.
findings.baseline_evidence: Actual baseline main compiled with a config_load wrapper inserting an owned 0600 file after a missing result. --init-config exited 0 and replaced the competitor (63 bytes became 1236 bytes).
findings.fix: New config_create() validates and publishes a complete 0600 temporary inode with same-directory linkat; --init-config uses it. Existing objects and publication races fail without replacing the destination. Ordinary explicit Save retains atomic replacement.
findings.fixed_evidence: The identical CLI wrapper caused fixed --init-config to exit 1 and preserve all 63 competitor bytes and mode 0600. Syscall-boundary regression tests also cover regular, symlink and FIFO competitors appearing immediately before publication.
findings.postpublication: Temporary cleanup or directory-sync failure returns an explicit created-but-failed diagnostic, leaving completed final data. The final destination is never unlinked by this operation.
findings.portability: No Linux-specific renameat2 flag. POSIX.1-2008 linkat uses the same pinned directory on both sides. Unsupported hard-link filesystems fail safely; no replacing fallback.

regression_target.note: The test includes config.c under narrow publication fault hooks; do not link config.c twice.

source_review: config.c/config.h: bounded literal config parser, transactional hotkey table validation, duplicate aliases, command-usage/private-path traversal, exact-mode secret reads, profile catalogs, ordinary atomic replacement, new exclusive create.

credentials.c: executable resolution without shell fallback, child descriptor isolation, SIGCHLD ownership, supervised process groups, bounded output/status, protected success markers, cancellation, literal password line validation, private encrypted-file publication/rollback.

background.c: account-private registry and lease use, incarnation-token controls, descriptor transfers and terminal validation, bounded requests/replies/deadlines, stale cleanup, child ownership, no numeric-PID guessing.
client.c: primary hotkey preference ownership, secondary inheritance/reload, save-before-apply behavior, stable session tokens, config copying/wiping.

main.c: inherited standard-fd reservation, UID/GID admission, core/dumpability protection, config-before-credential ordering, CLI endpoint reset and native signal preferences, managed session CLI separation.
reviewed_nonfindings: New hotkey storage contains only canonical keys and 20 allowlisted local action IDs, remains empty by default and is bounded to 64 rows. File duplicate aliases fail atomically. No command strings, arbitrary IRC payloads, shell commands, or secret values can be supplied as actions.

Filesystem paths already reject symlink traversal for private config/credentials. Reads validate ownership/file type/mode; private writes pin an owned private directory. Same-UID processes and the host remain trusted per project model.

GPG helper lifecycle still rejects automatic SIGCHLD reaping and retains a waitable leader until inherited output/status pipes finish; cancellation can safely target the owned group. Deliberately escaped descendants remain outside the documented helper contract.

Native socketpair and real SCM_RIGHTS tests reject excess/missing/malformed descriptors, wrong tokens, unsupported control metadata, and non-TTY devices without descriptor leaks. This is not pathname session listener coverage.

GCC -fanalyzer emitted one fd-leak warning in reserve_standard_descriptors(): the /dev/null descriptor intentionally becomes standard fd 0, 1 or 2 and remains open for the process lifetime (including after a later reservation failure, when main exits). This is an intentional ownership transfer, not a leaked application resource. Other reviewed local modules produced no analyzer diagnostics.

references.basis: Atomic creation, EEXIST, same-filesystem requirement, linkat descriptor-relative behavior; documentation verification, not native OpenBSD execution.
Existing destination is not overwritten; linkat and error behavior.

limitations: No cross-account attack, remote exploit, or code execution demonstrated for the no-clobber finding; impact is local configuration integrity.
Linux tests only; native OpenBSD/LibreSSL runtime not available.
Real GPG keyrings and real credentials were not exercised. Child lifecycle tests use private fake-helper executables with real fork/exec/pipe/signal operations.
ASan/UBSan tests used detect_leaks=0 because LeakSanitizer is incompatible with this host tracing environment; no leak-sanitizer-success claim.
No pathname AF_UNIX listener lifecycle is claimed; socketpair/SCM_RIGHTS and isolated production state/lease/control fixtures are distinguished.
No live IRCNow, bouncer account, production config, or pre-existing session was touched.
This review is not a proof that no vulnerabilities remain.

findings.fix: One shared post-paste/action gate covers ordinary keys, shortcuts, direct Run/send, mouse and modal consumers; requires later input batch, successful visible redraw and a quiet interval. Rejected repeats extend that interval.

findings.impact: A paste-closing marker followed by double Escape could reset Enter-only protection and execute an appended client command.
findings.fix: All suffix keys pass a common review gate before input-owner changes. Both shared idle.c files match.

findings.impact: A tiny-terminal notice could count as displaying a pasted command and allow execution without showing the draft.
findings.proof: pre-fix-idle-pty.json: old actual binary exits after hidden pasted /quit at4x10
findings.fix: Credit requires a complete editor/setup frame and fully drained output. Resize, interrupted terminal and failed/pending output retain protection.

independent_review_corrections_before_re: Retry full UI refresh after transient failure; a discarded mouse event requests another redraw.
Discarded guided-setup suffix keys still extend the deferred-result timer; result and cross-server Ui switch receive a new review gate.
Minimalist success/failure setup reset preserves the armed paste gate; WATCH requires its result notice/output to drain and recovers without inbound traffic.
record.validation_scope: Actual onekeyirc and vipirc -i PTYs. Full UI state uses a private non-ABI curses declaration shim and aborting renderer; no native full-curses build, rendering or physical-key validation. Full native test_status_mouse.c/test_integration.py were updated for fresh activation but could not be executed here.
limits: No public IRC servers, real accounts or real credentials used.
Asynchronous minimal setup tests use private helper fixtures and loopback servers with PING checks.
Full UI async tests stage a completed result in the actual guided state machine; do not run a real GPG job.
LeakSanitizer remains disabled because this host is ptraced.
No claim of unhackability; bracketed input markers and unframed typing remain terminal trust assumptions.
